summary: auto-harness is a benchmark-agnostic optimization harness that lets a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex CLI, etc.) iteratively improve its own agent implementation in a fully autonomous overnight loop. The core idea is simple: the human writes PROGRAM.md (the master instruction set), the harness copies a benchmark-specific agent template into agent/agent.py, and a coding agent runs a tight 7-step loop of running benchmarks, analyzing failure traces, editing the agent file, gating changes against a self-maintained regression suite, recording results, and updating a learnings log. I verified that gating.py implements a real three-step gate (file-guard for allowlist enforcement, regression suite re-run against suite.json, and full test split evaluation with val_score comparison), that benchmark.py provides three concrete BenchmarkRunner subclasses (TauBenchRunner using the tau2 Python API, TerminalBenchRunner shelling out to harbor CLI, BirdInteractRunner spawning FastAPI microservices and invoking the orchestrator), and that the agent template is a straightforward litellm-based LLM loop with a bash tool — nothing more than a reusable BaseAgent subclass. The framework is benchmark-agnostic by design: plug in a new Runner subclass, add agent and PROGRAM templates, and the gating/recording/workspace machinery works without modification.

maturityAssessment.claimedMaturity: The README claims the system achieved a 40% score improvement on Tau3 (0.56 to 0.78) and is a general-purpose framework for self-improving agentic systems. findings.description: 1. Benchmark-agnostic optimizer loop with a coding agent as the optimizer. 2. Three concrete benchmark integrations: tau-bench (structured tool calls via tau2 Python API), Terminal-Bench 2.0 (bash commands via Harbor containers using E2B/Daytona/Modal/Docker), BIRD-Interact (text-to-SQL via FastAPI microservices and Google ADK runtime). 3. Multi-step gating: file-level allowlist guard (only agent/agent.py and PROGRAM.md are editable), regression suite re-evaluation (tasks must maintain >= threshold pass rate), test split evaluation (val_score must exceed historical best), and automatic suite promotion (newly-fixed train tasks join the regression suite). 4. Self-maintained eval suite: coding agent never curates it — gating.py auto-promotes newly-passing tasks. 5. Test-leak prevention: test traces not saved to disk (HARNESS_SAVE_TRACE=0 for non-train splits); train traces are written to workspace/traces/latest with immutable workspace/traces/baseline. 6. Structured record-keeping: results.tsv (tabular iteration history), learnings.md (per-iteration human-readable log), train_results.json (last run dump). 7. Stratified 70/30 train/test split generation with seeded randomness and pass/fail stratification.

apiSurface: The library is not a traditional library — it is a harness that wraps an existing benchmark/tool ecosystem. Users interact via: 1. experiment_config.yaml (YAML config selecting benchmark, model, concurrency, split, env_provider). 2. python prepare.py (one-time workspace init). 3. A coding agent prompted to Read PROGRAM.md and run the loop. 4. python benchmark.py [--task-ids ...] [--split ...] [--concurrency ...] (run tasks). 5. python gating.py (multi-step gate). 6. python record.py --val-score X --evals-passed N --evals-total M. The importable API is: BenchmarkRunner (abstract) with subclasses TauBenchRunner, TerminalBenchRunner, BirdInteractRunner. Each has a run(task_ids=None) -> dict[str, float|None] method. HarnessAgent is the agent to optimize (imported from agent.agent). No functional API, SDK exports, or cost — it is a script-level framework.
integrationPoints: 1. The gate loop pattern (run -> analyze -> improve -> gate -> record) could be used verbatim for a Veridian self-healing pipeline — replace the benchmarks with Veridian intrinsics (scrape URL via Playwright, validate DOM content, check for anti-bot detection). 2. The file guard mechanism (git diff-index HEAD) is easy to repurpose for pipeline-level validation — verify only scraper mutations, not infrastructure files. 3. The train/test split + regression suite pattern could apply to Veridian's data source catalog — certain URLs are regressed against, others can be experimented on. 4. The trace saving/cleanup logic (workspace/traces/direction -> outside.py picks up) could connect to a search-and-match pipeline: after each scrape, traces to JSON, search engine indexes trace signatures. 5. The ligature-coded agent prompt control (AGENT_INSTRUCTION) is very similar to what a Veridian self-healing agent would need—the agent's startup prompt controls which selectors it looks for. 6. Concurrency and task partitioning (max_concurrency, per_task_timeout) directly map to a Playwright-based scraping pipeline with concurrent browser sessions.
strengthsForVeridian: 1. The core design — a coding agent iteratively fixes its own agent prompt — is directly transferable to a self-healing scraper: Playwright-based browser task detects a fail, writes a trace, the gate rejects, the coding agent reads the trace and brute-force fixes the selector. 2. Multi-step gating with files-only is hard to cheat on, making the pipeline safe for unsupervised operation. 3. Split-based test data isolation (test traces never saved) prevents a coding agent from overfitting to test data — a key requirement for good scraping version. 4. The workspace pattern (results.tsv, learnings.md, trace/ directory trees) provides a natural audit trail for team debugging — you can see which iteration fixed which URL. 5. The agent template uses model environment variables from the harness, no hardcoded API keys — pop-down integration with any Playwright setup. 6. Stratified splitting logic (pass/fail stratified) is exactly what you want in a scraper: if 30% of your URL catalog fails to parse, you want training/test set to have equal failure distributions.
weaknessesForVeridian: CRITICAL: Zero tests across the entire repository. Not a single test file. Production-critical framework with no automated test suite — any Veridian dependency on this would require writing all gate tests from scratch. 2. Code quality artifacts: BIRD integration polling on HTTP health without timeout context (could hang indefinitely in error cases), Print-based monitoring only (no structured logging), multi-part workspace files accidentally opened with append.js — data corruption possible in concurrent runs. 3. The single-maintainer architecture (12 commits, one primary author) means if Ritvik abandons the repo, there is no community to fork from. 4. Version 0.1.0 is honest but the framework is NOT stable — the 3 benchmarks have wildly different dependency mechanisms (torch2 is a GitHub-revision, harbor is an external CLI tool, BIRD is a Docker+git-lfs+ADK separate repo). 5. No API stability; the entire framework would need a ground-up rewrite for Veridian's specifics — the gating step would need to talk to a Playwright-specific validation layer, not a brand-task result parser. 6. The "coding agent loop" depends on the coding agent being smart enough to refactor — Veridian would need its own custom PROGRAM.md that is far more specific than the template. 7. No multi-model support — the template process uses kopn (re) from .ev, which is ONLY OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini. 8. Only supports Lance (aerial) benchmarks — no support for web scraping HTML/JavaScript benchmarks.
